_comment: Everything the utility policy weighs, in one file — 2e-ii. Mounted by Config under the 'ai' section, so these read as cfg.f("ai.weights.hull_down", ...) and a mistyped path lands in cfg.missing like any other. Scores are dimensionless utility; only their ratios matter. One point is roughly 'one tile of progress toward the objective' (weights.progress_per_tile is the yardstick the others are priced against).
_weights_note: Positive is attractive, negative is repellent — the sign is data, not code, so 'investigate sounds' versus 'avoid sounds' is a retune rather than a rewrite. hull_down/masked are per known enemy that cannot draw a clean bead on the tile; arc_threat is per known enemy whose turret is laid within the overwatch arc of it and can see it, which is the only overwatch fact a side can honestly know (the enemy's watch ORDER is hidden, its turret is not — docs/decisions/0036 withholds the wedge, not the gun).
_candidates_note: The hard cap 2e-ii asks for: a 30-unit turn has to resolve under a second, and the cap is what makes that a promise rather than a hope. Sampling is a deterministic stride over the reachable set in tile order — no draw, so the AI stream stays tie-break-only. contacts_considered bounds the LOS rays per candidate; the nearest few enemies dominate the danger anyway.
_tie_break_note: Candidates within epsilon of the best score are a tie, resolved by one draw from Rng.Stream.AI — the stream's only use, as 2e-ii specifies. Epsilon well below one point of utility: ties are for genuinely interchangeable tiles, not a blur radius.
